info.name: AI Agent — RAG API
info.description:
Document ingestion and vector search for the AI Agent Service (`/api/rag`).

## Before you start

1. Set the collection variable `base_url` (default `http://localhost:8000`).
2. Set `agent_api_token` to the value of **AGENT_API_TOKEN** in your `.env`.
   Note: that file defines the key twice — the LAST occurrence is the one the
   service uses. Copying the wrong one gives `401 Invalid or missing bearer token`.

Auth is set once on the collection (Bearer) and inherited by every request, so
no request carries its own header.

## Order to run in

**Service health** → **Upload document** (captures `document_id` automatically)
→ **Search** / **Context** → **List** → **Delete**.

The upload request needs a real file: open its Body tab and select one, since
Postman cannot store file contents inside a collection.

variable.description: AGENT_API_TOKEN from .env — the LAST occurrence of the key.
Set automatically by Upload document; used by Get and Delete.
The question the search and context requests ask.

request.description: The pre-existing liveness probe. Unauthenticated — if this fails, the service is down rather than the token being wrong.

exec: // ok is false until BOTH halves are ready, so it is the one flag to read.
pm.test('model width matches the pgvector column', () =>

request.description:
Whether the RAG layer is usable, and why not if it is not.

Reports configuration names and numbers only — never a DSN, never a key.
Always answers 200, including when unusable: a non-200 here would read as the whole service being down.

- `database.schema_ready` false ⇒ run `python -m app.rag.migrate`
- `embeddings.loaded` false ⇒ the embedding server is unreachable or misconfigured
- `ok` true ⇒ uploads and searches will work

formdata.description: REQUIRED. A .pdf, .docx or .txt. Open this tab and select the file — Postman cannot store file contents in a collection.
Optional. Your own id (a Laravel media id, a hash). Generated when omitted. Re-using an existing id is a primary-key conflict — delete first.
Optional scope. Searches can be filtered by it later.
Optional JSON OBJECT, sent as a string because multipart cannot carry JSON. Anything else is a 422.

request.description:
Ingest one document: extract → clean → chunk → embed → store.

Only `file` is required; the four optional fields are disabled by default — enable the ones you actually scope by.

Synchronous by design: the response tells you how many chunks were stored, and a failure is a failed request rather than a job that quietly never finished. A large PDF therefore takes as long as it takes to embed.

**Status codes**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| 201 | Ingested |
| 400 | Unsupported file type (only pdf, docx, txt) |
| 413 | Larger than `RAG_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` |
| 422 | Empty file, no extractable text, or bad `metadata` JSON |
| 502 | The embedding backend failed |
| 503 | `RAG_DATABASE_URL` unset, or the parser is not installed |

A scanned PDF gives 422: it holds images, not text, and OCR is not enabled.

response.name: 400 — unsupported file type

exec: // found=false is a valid answer, not a failure: nothing reached the
// threshold. The calling agent decides what to do about it.
pm.test('every result is above the threshold', () =>

request.description:
Embed the query, rank chunks in Postgres, return those above the threshold.

**No LLM is called.** This returns chunks, not an answer.

**Optional fields** (add to the body as needed)

```json
{
  "query": "What is the refund policy?",
  "top_k": 5,
  "threshold": 0.5,
  "user_id": "42",
  "agent_id": "support",
  "conversation_id": "c-1",
  "document_ids": ["doc_9f2c…"]
}
```

- `top_k` — defaults to `RAG_TOP_K`, capped at `RAG_MAX_TOP_K` (50). 0 or negative is a 422.
- `threshold` — overrides `RAG_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` for this call. 0 disables the filter, which is the quickest way to see the raw scores while tuning.
- the scope fields and `document_ids` narrow the search; omit them to search everything.

**On the scores:** BGE-M3 similarities sit in a narrow band — a correct match is around 0.6, not 0.9, and unrelated text still scores about 0.4. Set the threshold between those two clusters, measured on your own documents.

**Status codes** — 422 empty query or bad `top_k` · 502 embedding backend · 503 storage not configured.

response.name: 200 — found

request.description:
The same retrieval as Search, assembled into one block of text with its sources.

Accepts everything Search accepts, plus `max_chars` (defaults to `RAG_CONTEXT_MAX_CHARS`).

Chunks are numbered and labelled — `[1] policy.pdf, page 4` — so a prompt can cite them and the model can tell two documents apart inside one block. Whole chunks only: a chunk that would exceed the budget is dropped rather than truncated, because half a sentence in a prompt reads as a fact that was never written.

**This endpoint calls no LLM and touches no agent code.** It exists so the existing agent can fetch context when it decides to — paste `context` into your system prompt, or send it in the `context` field of `/agent/reply`.

response.name: 200 — context assembled

request.description:
Documents, newest first, paginated.

`total` is the count for the same filter, not for the page — page through with `offset`.

One document record. `{{document_id}}` is set automatically by the Upload request.

404 if it does not exist.

Delete the document, its chunks and their embeddings.

One transaction: either all of it goes or none of it does. A half-deleted document would leave chunks that still answer searches while their document record no longer exists.

404 if the id is unknown.
